headline: Kai, a 165,000-payroll surprise put a December Fed hike in play, and Friday's chip rebound couldn't save the S&P from a 2.7% week.
subline: Democrats' House majority is heading toward 257 seats, bitcoin is holding the $75,000 line, and October CPI lands Tuesday.
asof: Weekend edition · built Saturday ~6:50 AM ET · strip shows Friday's close · every figure links to its source below

items.title: Chips bounce, but the week still closed red
items.sentence: The S&P 500 rose 0.3% Friday to 7,376.86 and the Nasdaq gained 1.1% as chip stocks rebounded, but the Dow fell 237.33 points and the S&P still lost 2.7% on the week, per the AP.

items.title: October payrolls nearly triple the forecast
items.sentence: Employers added 165,000 jobs against roughly 59,000 expected and unemployment fell to 4.1%, and traders now put the odds of a December Fed hike above 65%, per Stock Titan's live blog citing the BLS and CME FedWatch.

items.title: Yields and oil settle higher; gold slips
items.sentence: The 10-year Treasury rose 2.3 basis points to settle at 4.858%, December gold fell 0.94% to $4,074.90, and WTI crude settled at $90.83 with Brent at $98.32, per Hammerstone Markets' recap on Investrade.

items.title: Bitcoin holds the $75,000 shelf
items.sentence: Bitcoin steadied near $75,500 after Thursday's 5.2% drop — a move that liquidated more than $1.27 billion in crypto positions and pulled $430.2 million from spot ETFs in a day — with Wintermute's desk flagging $73,000 and $68,000 as the next supports, per Forex Crunch.

items.title: CPI Tuesday, PPI Friday, Cisco Thursday
items.sentence: October CPI lands Tuesday morning and PPI follows Friday, while Cisco and Applied Materials headline Thursday's earnings alongside CoreWeave on Tuesday and Constellation Energy on Monday, per Stock Titan's calendar.

items.title: Democrats pad the House; Senate rests on two states
items.sentence: Democrats hold 253 House seats with counting still under way and are expected to finish near 257, while Senate control turns on razor-thin leads for Scott Colom in Mississippi and Mary Peltola in Alaska, per Everything Briefing's tallies.

items.title: Trump nears a decision on resuming Iran strikes
items.sentence: President Trump said he will decide soon whether to resume military action against Iran now that the midterms are over, as Tehran routed a new nuclear proposal through Qatar, per Axios and Reuters items in Just Security's roundup.

items.title: A Kremlin envoy gets a White House meeting
items.sentence: Trump met Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev at the White House and spoke of a Ukraine peace deal that might involve all of Europe, while Zelenskyy said Kyiv must adapt to Washington's new politics, per NYT and Reuters via Just Security.

items.title: Paraguay's president resigns over a bank seizure
items.sentence: Santiago Peña resigned after Paraguay's central bank seized Ueno Bank, a digital lender claiming more than 60% of the country's adults as customers, per New York Times reporting in Just Security's roundup.

items.title: Anthropic's IPO price talk drops by a third
items.sentence: Investors now peg Anthropic's imminent listing at $1 trillion to $1.3 trillion, down from roughly $2 trillion a month ago, and prediction-market odds of a debut before December 1 have slid from about 80% to 50%, per Yahoo Finance.

items.title: OpenAI ships GPT-6 Cyber and calls it Critical
items.sentence: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Cyber, a model that lets vetted researchers find vulnerabilities and build exploits to test defenses, rating its cyber capabilities Critical and restricting initial access to selected organizations, per The Neuron.

items.title: Claude will read your bank account, if asked
items.sentence: Anthropic opened a Claude Personal Finance beta that links US Pro, Max and Ultra accounts read-only through Plaid and can review up to two years of transactions, per The Neuron.

items.title: Google commits $17 billion to a Wyoming campus
items.sentence: Google announced a $17 billion Wyoming data center leaning partly on a planned 702-megawatt fuel-cell development, even as governments from New York to Amsterdam tighten data-center rules, per The Neuron.

items.title: Justice Department opens an AI enforcement front
items.sentence: The DOJ stood up a Super Intelligence Task Force to investigate unlawful uses of advanced AI by foreign governments, criminal organizations and fraudsters, per The Neuron.
